answer: Policies are written in signal, settled in trellis, and wharf lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 19% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 166 aliases cost 332 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
